1. Core Clinical Tension: A young adult presenting with dense aphasia and hemiplegia on the background of prolonged fevers, splenic granulomas, and abdominal lymphadenitis initially treated empirically for presumed mycobacterial tuberculosis. The rapid multi-compartment intracranial suppuration (concomitant epidural collection, subdural empyema, and intraparenchymal ring-enhancing abscess) despite empiric multi-drug coverage creates intense clinical tension between refractory CNS tuberculosis, pyogenic polymicrobial abscess, and neurotropic tropical pathogens.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission triage narrative concludes when the patient is evaluated at our center with physical examination demonstrating altered sensorium and dense right hemiplegia, alongside multi-sequence brain MRI showing multi-compartment purulent collections, immediately prior to surgical craniectomy and microbiological/histopathological analysis.
3. Differential Distinctions: CNS tuberculosis typically manifests with basal meningeal enhancement, tuberculomas, or vasculitic infarcts without massive multi-compartment purulence. Pyogenic brain abscesses usually arise from adjacent sinonasal or otogenic foci rather than indolent splenic granulomas and multi-compartment suppuration. Cerebral melioidosis characteristically presents with aggressive multi-compartment intracranial suppurative collections, often mimicking tuberculosis in endemic regions.
case_prompt:
A 24-year-old male presented to the emergency department with global aphasia and right-sided hemiplegia. Four months prior, he began experiencing intermittent headaches. Three months prior to presentation, he developed an evening rise in temperature and abdominal pain. He sought treatment at an outside institution where evaluation with abdominal ultrasound revealed splenomegaly with multiple granulomas; abdominal computed tomography (CT) confirmed these findings and further demonstrated periportal, para-aortic, and aortocaval lymphadenopathy. He was empirically initiated on multi-drug antimicrobial therapy for presumed granulomatous lymphadenitis. Ten days later, his symptoms worsened with new-onset speech difficulty and right-sided weakness; subsequent brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a thin left frontal subdural collection (measuring approximately 2 × 3 × 2 mm, volume 6 mm³) and a rim of thin epidural collection, and his empiric regimen was maintained.

Over the subsequent month, his neurological deficits progressed to complete expressive speech loss and dense hemiplegia, prompting transfer to our center. On physical examination, he was in an altered sensorium with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 12 (E3V4M5) and dense right-sided hemiplegia. Cranial MRI demonstrated a complex left frontal intraparenchymal lesion featuring an isointense rim with hypointense collection on T1-weighted images, fluid-fluid levels on T2-weighted images, hyperintense extra-axial and subdural collections on T2/FLAIR sequences, and conglomerate peripheral ring enhancement on post-contrast sequences. The intraparenchymal mass was accompanied by significant perilesional edema with marked mass effect compressing the ipsilateral frontal horn and body of the lateral ventricle. Diffusion-weighted imaging demonstrated diffusion restriction within the lesion capsule and dependent purulent debris, and magnetic resonance spectroscopy demonstrated markedly elevated lipid-lactate peaks. Findings indicated a multi-compartment suppurative process consisting of intraparenchymal cerebral abscess, subdural empyema, and epidural abscess, with associated left frontal cortical vein thrombosis.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the indolent presentation, abdominal lymphadenopathy, and splenic granulomas; however, the patient deteriorated with rapidly expanding multi-compartment suppuration (epidural, subdural, and parenchymal abscesses) while receiving dedicated anti-tubercular therapy, and surgical cultures grew Burkholderia pseudomallei.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: evaluated with ultrasound abdomen that showed splenomegaly with multiple granulomas and the findings were later confirmed with computerized tomography (CT) abdomen which also revealed periportal, para-aortic, and aortic caval lymphadenitis-like features, for which he was treated presumptively as a mycobacterial tuberculosis infection. Ten days later, the symptoms worsened and the patient developed new-onset speech difficulty along with right-sided weakness.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered because neuroimaging showed marked diffusion restriction and lipid-lactate peaks consistent with purulent bacterial infection; however, typical pyogenic brain abscesses arise acutely from contiguous sinus or otic sources or acute endocarditis, unlike this patient's subacute 4-month course with splenic granulomas and extensive three-compartment suppuration.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Findings favored infective etiology with cerebral abscess, subdural empyema, and dural thickening with an intradural abscess in the left frontal region with frontal cortical vein thrombosis.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Decompressive craniectomy with surgical evacuation of purulent material across the epidural, subdural, and parenchymal compartments revealed viable Burkholderia pseudomallei on microbiological culture and histopathology, confirming cerebral melioidosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The patient underwent left fronto-temporo-parietal decompressive craniectomy and abscess evacuation... The histopathology and culture evaluation grew B. pseudomallei, subsequently, he was started on intravenous antibiotics

All pathogen and disease names are completely excluded from the clinical presentation narrative. Direct quotes from the source text are 100% verbatim.
